question: What exactly is an occupational health hazard?

options.A: The personal medical history of a factory worker
options.B: Only physical injuries sustained during a night shift
options.C: A financial loss experienced by a business owner
options.D: Any workplace factor that can cause injury or illness

explanation: Think of an occupational hazard as anything at work—like dust, noise, or stress—that can harm a worker's body or mind. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses care so much about spotting workplace hazards early?

options.A: It stops short-term injuries and long-term chronic illnesses
options.B: It guarantees higher daily wages for industrial workers
options.C: It removes the need for personal protective equipment
options.D: It completely eliminates all physical labor in factories

explanation: Catching risks early means we can protect workers before they get seriously hurt. Prevention is always better than cure! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h1)

question: Loud factory noise and extreme heat belong to which hazard category?
explanation: Physical hazards are environmental forces like noise, vibration, and extreme temperatures that interact directly with our bodies. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h2)

question: A nurse checks a poorly arranged office desk that causes chronic back strain. What kind of hazard is this?
explanation: Ergonomic hazards happen when the workspace or tools do not fit the natural posture and movement of the human body. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h2)

question: What health problem is most directly linked to working near loud industrial machinery without ear protection?
explanation: Constant high noise damages the delicate inner ear over time, leading to permanent hearing loss. Ear protection is a lifesaver! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h3)

question: A farmer who sprays crops without protection starts feeling dizzy and shaky. What is the likely cause?
explanation: Pesticides are powerful chemicals that can easily enter the body during spraying and trigger toxic symptoms like dizziness and tremors. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h3)

question: Which group of workers faces the highest daily risk of exposure to bloodborne infections like HIV and Hepatitis B?
explanation: As nurses, doctors, and lab staff handling needles and body fluids daily, we are right on the front line for bloodborne risks. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h4)

question: Why do market porters who carry heavy loads on their heads often suffer from chronic back and neck pain?

options.A: They suffer from acute biological infections spread by insects
options.B: They experience psychosocial stress from working long hours
options.C: They are exposed to dangerous chemical solvents in the market
options.D: They face severe ergonomic strain from heavy lifting and poor posture

explanation: Balancing heavy loads incorrectly puts immense pressure on the spine and supporting muscles, leading to long-term pain. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h4)

question: What is the main goal of doing a Job Safety Analysis (JSA)?

options.A: Conducting routine blood pressure checks on factory workers
options.B: Calculating the monthly profit margin of an industrial plant
options.C: Breaking down a task step-by-step to spot hidden dangers
options.D: Measuring the exact decibel levels of factory machinery

explanation: A JSA looks at every little step of a job to catch safety risks before someone gets hurt. Teamwork makes safety work! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h5)

question: What do we call it when a nurse physically walks through a factory floor to observe how safe the workers' habits are?
explanation: A workplace walkthrough lets healthcare pros see real working conditions and habits firsthand so we can help keep workers safe. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h5)

question: Why is asking about a patient's job so important during a health assessment?

options.A: It proves the employer is legally guilty of negligence
options.B: It determines the exact salary the worker earns each month
options.C: It replaces the need for standard physical examinations
options.D: It links patient symptoms to exposures in their workplace

explanation: Many illnesses build up slowly over time. Knowing what a patient does for a living helps us connect the dots to their health issues. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h6)

question: A patient has a cough that gets worse during workdays but clears up completely on weekends. What should you suspect?

options.A: An acute infection caught during weekend travel
options.B: A symptom unrelated to lifestyle or environment
options.C: An occupational exposure in the work environment

explanation: When symptoms flare up only during work hours and ease during rest days, it's a huge clue that something at work is causing it. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h6)

question: What is one of the main duties of a community health nurse regarding occupational safety?

options.A: Educating workers on hazard recognition and protective gear
options.B: Designing industrial machinery for manufacturing companies
options.C: Enforcing labor laws through police intervention
options.D: Managing the financial accounts of private factories

explanation: Community nurses shine at health education—teaching everyday workers how to spot dangers and use protective gear correctly. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h7)

question: Why are community health nurses especially important for local mechanics, welders, and informal workers?

options.A: Informal workers never experience any health hazards on the job
options.B: Informal workers often lack formal safety training and access to corporate health clinics
options.C: Community nurses have direct authority to close down dangerous workshops
options.D: Informal workers are legally prohibited from visiting standard hospitals

explanation: Since informal workers don't have corporate safety clinics, community health nurses step in as their trusted source of health guidance. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h7)

question: What is the main benefit of keeping accurate records of workplace injuries and close calls?

options.A: It helps identify dangerous trends and prevents future accidents
options.B: It guarantees that the business will never face taxation
options.C: It allows employers to hide safety violations from inspectors
options.D: It replaces the need to provide medical treatment to victims

explanation: Reviewing past injury logs helps safety teams spot repeating problems so they can fix them before anyone else gets hurt. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a good reason for a nurse to log every workplace injury?

options.A: To provide data for spotting workplace hazard patterns
options.B: To punish workers who report minor pain or discomfort
options.C: To help employers improve safety standards over time
options.D: To ensure injured workers can access proper medical care

explanation: Incident logs are meant to protect and care for workers, never to blame or punish them for speaking up about pain. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h8)
